title: Allison Janney on Playing the President in ‘The Diplomat,’ Her Broadway ‘Seven-Year Itch’ and the One Genre She’s Never Tried
description:
Allison Janney is shy, and she has no interest in ever being president. 

	The first part surprises people. The second is now professionally inconve
body:
Allison Janney is shy, and she has no interest in ever being president. 

	The first part surprises people. The second is now professionally inconvenient because Janney has spent the better part of two decades walking the corridors of a fictional Washington, D.C., and finally has taken the seat behind the Oval Office desk. In “The Diplomat,” Debora Cahn’s political thriller on Netflix, Janney’s Grace Penn has ascended from vice president to commander in chief, a turn the actor swears she did not see coming. “I didn’t know until I read the last page of a script,” Janney tells Variety. “I was sitting right here in my kitchen and turned the page and saw it, and it just freaked me out. I haven’t had that kind of reaction to a script before, ever.”
	

	We are talking over Zoom, Janney at a desk in her home office, a pool visible behind her. Walking around her and then hopping onto her lap is Lilo, a pit bull her niece is fostering. It is a domestic scene entirely at odds with the woman she plays. I met Janney almost a decade ago at the after party for “I, Tonya,” Craig Gillespie’s 2017 biopic, following its screening at the New York Film Festival. In my early pundit days, I walked up to her and told her flat-out she was going to win an Oscar. She said, in so many words, “You’re kind, but that’s not happening.” A few months later she won the Academy Award for supporting actress as LaVona Golden, the abusive mother of figure skater Tonya Harding (Margot Robbie).


	Nine years later, the seven-time Emmy winner has her latest nomination, for supporting drama actress, and “The Diplomat” has its strongest awards haul yet, with seven total bids, including for co-stars Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell, and a drama series nom. A win would place her alongside Cloris Leachman and Julia Louis-Dreyfus in the record books as the most awarded female performer in history, a prospect she waves off with characteristic dryness. “Sure, those hacks,” she deadpans.
	

	Nonetheless, Janney has recently wrapped Season 4, which she calls “a doozy,” and does not sugarcoat where it leaves everyone. “Both marriages are in trouble,” she reveals. Grace and Hal Wyler (Rufus Sewell) have done something “morally, politically questionable.” As of the close of Season 3, Kate Wyler (Keri Russell) knows about it. “Kate is the smartest woman in the room, and she now knows their secret,” Janney says. “Going into Season 4, that could not be great for a lot of people.”

	The fallout, she suggests, reaches well past the marriages. “This new thing they’ve done is creating more tension and could create more tension between the U.K. and the U.S., and possibly Russia, and sets us up for a potential war scenario. They’ve done something very, very dark.” She repeatedly declines to say what it is.

	Then, later discussing whether C.J. Cregg, her character on “The West Wing,” would recognize Grace Penn, she may have dropped a hint sideways: C.J., she says, “wouldn’t be willing to steal a nuclear sub.”



	

					The Diplomat. (L to R) Allison Janney as Grace Penn, Rufus Sewell as Hal Wyler, Nana Mensah as Billie Appiah, Keri Russell as Kate Wyler in episode 306 of The Diplomat. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2025
									Courtesy of Netflix
	



	The show’s inauguration sequence landed harder than anyone on set anticipated. It was shot not long after the 2024 election results, and the mood was eerie. “Everyone got kind of emotional about it,” Janney recalls. “It was that our country can’t seem to get behind putting a woman in that office.”

	The irony is that Janney has now played two of television’s most formidable Washington women and identifies with neither. When told she’d make a fine candidate herself, she cuts the idea at the knees, going back to my initial prediction that she’d win the Oscar. “That is one thing I’m going to tell you you’re wrong about,” she asserts. “I love playing strong women with huge flaws or huge secrets. But in real life, I am not that at all. I am shy. I do not like to speak in front of people. I am not these characters at all, and all my friends will tell you that too.”

	She credits Cahn’s dense dialogue that’s so packed it has become the show’s signature tempo. But what impresses her most is what Cahn chooses to withhold. In one scene, Janney and Bradley Whitford, who plays her husband, Todd, get ready for bed after a fight without a word between them, then curl up together anyway. “Her writing gives actors so much to work with, and then she also trusts us to have no dialogue,” she says. “That was a beautiful scene.”
	

	Weeks after the upcoming Emmys, Janney will open on Broadway in Jon Robin Baitz’s play “Other Desert Cities,” which runs from Oct. 18 through Jan. 17 . She stars opposite Louis-Dreyfus, Ed Harris, Lily Rabe and Joe Keery. It’s her first stage appearance since “Six Degrees of Separation” seven years ago; she calls it her seven-year itch. “Acting is a team sport, and when you’re on stage, there’s nothing like being in front of a live audience,” she says.

	Theater, she believes, is why she was never typecast: “All the actors I love the most have come from the theater. All the ‘West Wing’ actors came from the theater.”

	Next on her docket is a role in Oscar-winning Justine Triet’s “Fonda,” which shot in France in February with Odessa A’zion and Andrew Scott. “I had the best time,” Janney says. “I know the way she’s editing it and the music; it’s going to be a really cool movie.”

	With a career that’s so adored and respected — her résumé ranges from “The Hours” to “Juno” — it’s no surprise fans stop her on the street to talk about their favorite roles, like “Drop Dead Gorgeous” and others that have surprised her. But alas, there are two roles she has yet to play.

	The first is a superhero, a want that is traceable back to her childhood spent watching the classic “Bewitched.” “I was determined that if I twitched the right body parts, I too could be magic,” she says.

	The second is the layup she’s yet to tackle: “I’ve never done a horror film before. That would be really fun.”

	Blumhouse, your move. 

	And somebody, go adopt Lilo.

schema.headline: Allison Janney on Playing the President in ‘The Diplomat,’ Her Broadway ‘Seven-Year Itch’ and the One Genre She’s Never Tried

title: Jerry Katzman, Former William Morris President, Dies at 89
description: Jerry Katzman, a former William Morris president and television packager for series such as “Roseanne” and “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” died on Au
body:
Jerry Katzman, a former William Morris president and television packager for series such as “Roseanne” and “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” died on Aug. 9. He was 89.

	Katzman helped shape modern television with his work in television packaging and bringing series to the screen, contributing to the success of shows such as “The Cosby Show” and “Murphy Brown.” He first joined William Morris in business affairs before rising to the head of worldwide television, then to president and vice chairman. 
	

	Also serving as the president of the Hollywood Radio and Television Society, Katzman later taught at UCLA’s School of Theater, Film and Television. In the early 1970s, he worked with his father in film production on projects including Elvis Presley’s “Kissin Cousins” and “Harum Scarum,” as well as Roy Orbison’s “Fastest Guitar Alive” and Peter Noone’s “Hold On!”. 


	Katzman was born April 21, 1937, in Los Angeles and was married to Carol Sinn for 66 years. “Jerry loved spending time with his kids and grandkids, and together with Carol never missed an opportunity to celebrate every birthday, anniversary, wedding, graduation and holiday,” his obituary reads. 

	He struggled with Parkinson’s for several years. In addition to his wife Carol, he is survived by his children, Jeff, Jon and Kari; seven grandchildren and a great-granddaughter. Donations may be made to: Jewish Federation in Los Angeles, Cedars Sinai Board of Governors and UCLA Parkinson’s Center: Attention Dr. Jeff Bronstein/Jessica Vrazilek.
	

	Services will be held on Aug. 13 at Hillside Memorial Park, 6001 W. Centinela Ave, Los Angeles, at noon.

schema.headline: Jerry Katzman, Former William Morris President, Dies at 89

title: AI Music Company Suno Unveils Download Caps for Free, Paid Tiers in Quest to Combat Abuse (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Suno last week said that it would impose download limits on users of its AI music generator as it seeks to legitimize its presence in the music indu
body:
Suno last week said that it would impose download limits on users of its AI music generator as it seeks to legitimize its presence in the music industry. Now it has specifics.

	Starting Sept. 3 for all songs in a user’s library, free Suno users will be limited to seven total downloads, while those on its $8-a-month Pro plan — which gives users the right to license their tracks for commercial use — will be limited to 20 downloads a month. For Suno users shelling out $24 a month for the company’s “Premier” tier, which provides access to its “Studio” production suite of generation tools, users will be given 60 downloads a month. Users eager to download more songs beyond their limits can purchase them, though no limits apply to users of Suno Studio. It is unclear how the limits will impact downloads for Suno’s upcoming vinyl program, which the company expects to unveil in the coming months.
	

	Suno said in a blog post Monday that the downloads are part of an effort to “make it harder for bad actors to mass-export music.” Spotify, Apple Music and other music streaming services have been open about their efforts to combat the proliferation of AI-generated music flooding their libraries, including those improperly uploaded to human artists’ pages and those trying to game the services’ systems. 


	“We are introducing download limits to ensure our platform is used for intentional music creation, while still allowing everyone to create, remix, listen, and share on Suno,” Suno said on Monday.

	The limits, which will apply to all songs in a user’s library, stemmed from the company’s settlement with Warner Music Group last year in the label’s copyright infringement lawsuit against the company. Udio last year disabled downloads completely as part of its own copyright infringement settlement with Universal Music Group. 
	

	Both Udio and Suno are working on respective models backed by their label partners, and Suno said on Monday that its new label-backed models “generate outputs faster, deliver higher fidelity audio, and give you more control over your music than ever before.”

	The limits were first teased last week in a blog post by CEO Mikey Shulman, who also said the company would begin watermarking songs downloaded from the platform to help signify the use of AI. The company is still being sued by UMG and Sony Music for copyright infringement, and a German court found last month that the company was violating U.S. and German copyright laws.

schema.headline: AI Music Company Suno Unveils Download Caps for Free, Paid Tiers in Quest to Combat Abuse (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Damon Wayans Reunites With ‘In Living Color’ Co-Star David Alan Grier in ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere
description: Damon Wayans will share the screen once again with his “In Living Color” castmate David Alan Grier with a guest appearance in the Season 3 premiere
body:
Damon Wayans will share the screen once again with his “In Living Color” castmate David Alan Grier with a guest appearance in the Season 3 premiere of “St. Denis Medical.”

	Wayans will play Dr. Highland, who is described as “a charming but pompous new doctor at St. Denis. He is filling in while Ron (Grier) is recovering from surgery. All the patients and staff, besides Alex (Allison Tolman) have fallen head over heels for him and his insights.” The episode will air on Nov. 2.
	

	“St. Denis Medical” is a mockumentary set in “an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the dedicated doctors and nurses try their best to treat patients while maintaining their own sanity,” per the official logline. The cast is led by Tolman, with Grier playing the grumpy emergency physician Ron. Wendi McLendon-Covey, Josh Lawson, Kahyun Kim, Mekki Leeper and Kaliko Kauahi also star. Justin Spitzer co-created the series with Eric Ledgin, who serves as showrunner. Both executive produce alongside Simon Heuer, Bridget Kyle and Vicky Luu. More Bees, Inc. and Spitzer Holding Company produce the series, while Universal Television is the studio.


	Grier was a cast member on all five seasons of “In Living Color,” which ran on Fox from 1990 to 1994, while Wayans starred in the first three seasons and recurred in Season 4. Wayans’ other best known credit is ABC’s “My Wife and Kids,” which he led alongside Tisha Campbell-Martin for five seasons from 2001 to 2005, and he more recently starred in Fox’s “Lethal Weapon” series for three seasons from 2016 to 2019. Wayans is repped by Verve.

schema.headline: Damon Wayans Reunites With ‘In Living Color’ Co-Star David Alan Grier in ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere

title: ‘Law and Order: SVU’ Best of Mariska Hargitay Marathon Set for September on NBC
description:
NBC is airing a “Law and Order: SVU” marathon in celebration of series mainstay Mariska Hargitay. 

	NBC will air three episodes of “SVU” back-to-ba
body:
NBC is airing a “Law and Order: SVU” marathon in celebration of series mainstay Mariska Hargitay. 

	NBC will air three episodes of “SVU” back-to-back on Sept. 10 featuring Hargitay’s Emmy-winning performance in the 2005 episode “911” as well as two other episodes for which she received Emmy nominations. The full lineup can be seen below. 

	The marathon comes four days ahead of the 2026 Emmy Awards, which will air on NBC with Hargitay set to host. She is the first woman to host the annual TV awards show in 15 years. 
	

	Hargitay has been a central cast member on “SVU” since the show launched in 1999. She has received eight total Emmy nominations for her role as Capt. Olivia Benson, as well as two Golden Globe noms with one win. She also now serves as an executive producer and director on the series. 


	In addition to her work on “SVU,” Hargitay received two Emmy nominations for the documentary “My Mom Jayne” — one for outstanding documentary or nonfiction special and another for outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program. 

	“Law and Order: SVU” will air its 28th season this fall, beginning Oct. 8. It is set to air its 600th episode later this year. Episodes stream the day after their linear debut on Peacock. 

	The series is executive produced by Dick Wolf, Michele Fazekas, Hargitay, Ken Brown, Rebecca McGill, Anastasia Puglisi and Peter Jankowski. It is produced by Universal Television in association with Wolf Entertainment.

	“Law & Order: SVU” Sept. 10 Marathon Lineup

	8 p.m. – “Charisma”(Emmy-nominated episode; originally aired Nov. 16, 2004)
	

	9 p.m. – “911” (Emmy-winning episode; originally aired Oct. 4, 2005)

	10 p.m. – “Undercover”(Emmy-nominated episode; originally aired April 15, 2008)

schema.headline: ‘Law and Order: SVU’ Best of Mariska Hargitay Marathon Set for September on NBC

title: UTA Signs ‘Forgotten Island’ Writer-Director Januel Mercado (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
United Talent Agency has signed rising filmmaker Januel Mercado for representation in all areas.

	Mercado is the writer and director of DreamWorks
body:
United Talent Agency has signed rising filmmaker Januel Mercado for representation in all areas.

	Mercado is the writer and director of DreamWorks Animation’s upcoming “Forgotten Island,” along with Joel Crawford. 

	Set in the 1990s, H.E.R. and Liza Soberano voice Jo and Raissa, two best friends who, post high-school, are about to go their separate ways. As they celebrate their last night together by eating junk food and singing karaoke, the pair stumble on a magical portal. The film also stars Lea Salonga, Dave Franco, Manny Jacinto and Jenny Slate.
	

	Most recently, Mercado served as co-director of DreamWorks Animation’s “Puss in Boots: The Last Wish alongside longtime creative collaborator Joel Crawford. The film became both a critical and commercial triumph, grossing nearly $500 million at the global box office while earning Golden Globe, Oscar and BAFTA Award nominations for Best Animated Feature.


	Mercado joined the studio’s story department in 2008 and contributed to beloved franchises including “Kung Fu Panda,” “Penguins of Madagascar,” “Turbo” and “Trolls,” before serving as head of story on “The Croods: A New Age.” His additional credits include Warner Bros. Animation’s LEGO franchise and a leadership role as supervising director at Nickelodeon Animation.

	Recognized as one of the industry’s rising creative voices, Mercado was among this year’s Variety and Gold House’s 8 APIs Up Next in Entertainment list. He told Variety that he roots himself in a nebula of core values: “Let love and passion lead the way. There is magic in hope and positivity. Also, you can’t do great things alone. It takes a village. Build community and inspire with art and authenticity.”
	

	On making “Forgotten Island,” Mercado hoped inspire with art and authenticity. “After working on many sequels and franchises together, we wanted to tell a story that not only celebrated the meaningful connections and memories that shape us, but also a film that honored our families and Filipino culture.”

	Mercado continues to be represented by Joann Mercado Hicks for management.

schema.headline: UTA Signs ‘Forgotten Island’ Writer-Director Januel Mercado (EXCLUSIVE)

title: How ‘Euphoria’ Makeup Artist Used Red Lips and Black Eyeliner to Reflect Jules’ Power, Maturity and Sexuality
description: Crystals, glitter and bold looks characterized “Euphoria’s” first two seasons, but when the show returned for its third and final season, the makeup
body:
Crystals, glitter and bold looks characterized “Euphoria’s” first two seasons, but when the show returned for its third and final season, the makeup shifted away from the sparkle, shimmer and intense looks that had defined the show. Season 3 saw a five-year time jump, which meant that Rue (Zendaya), Jules (Hunter Schafer), Cassie (Sydney Sweeney) and the rest of the cast were now young adults. Makeup artist Donni Davy needed to reflect that maturity through her craft.
	

	“It’s not about exploring who you are. It’s about gaining power, fame, recognition, money and control,” Davy explains. “It’s more feral, and there are things at stake.”


	With Jules, she doesn’t want to be in art school — she just wants to paint. “She finds a way to make money, and she’s trying on this lifestyle of being a sugar baby. It needed to cater to the male gaze.” In one scene, Davy gave Jules a red lip for a dinner with an older man. “Some of her looks are supposed to feel a little odd,” Davy says. “She’s trying to take something of hers that used to come so naturally, and she’s trying to tailor it to the male gaze and to this world that lacks color.”

	One element Davy loved was giving Jules black eyeliner under her eyes — a detail that’s a little baby doll-like. “It feels darker and more about sexuality with these men and turning herself over to them in exchange for money and comfort,” Davy explains.



	

									Patrick Wymore
	



	In contrast, Rue had nothing on her face. Creator/showrunner Sam Levinson didn’t want anything. Davy explains, “She’s sleeping in her car a lot. It’s not part of her priorities. Rue is surviving, trying to find a path toward getting some money and working herself up in the world. She’s lost.”
	



	

	



	Cassie, on the other hand, has dabbled in glam makeup and is always trying new things to get male attention. Davy says Cassie’s glam has changed this season: heavy eyeshadow, sparkle, contour, a sparkly lip and long clawlike nails — it’s all part of how she’s morphing. “That’s part of what she does,” Davy says. She’s a fledgling digital content creator, and in the season premiere, she dons a puppy dog outfit for clicks. Davy enhanced Cassie’s lips using a big lip liner and added fake freckles, a reflection of TikTok and Instagram trends.



	

	



	When Cassie discovers OnlyFans and ventures into that world, Davy notes, “Her look very quickly becomes more sexy and fierce.” But it doesn’t end there. Cassie’s hair becomes blonder, she’s tanned and “she’s pulling out all the stops to get as much attention as possible in Los Angeles.”

	Davy adds, “She’s taking on this Pam Anderson, Marilyn Monroe vibe. There’s a little bit of Brigitte Bardot for that pool photo shoot scene where she’s in the little red-and-white gingham outfit as she continues to try all these different looks to see how sexy she can possibly make herself.” And getting attention is Cassie’s ultimate goal.

schema.headline: How ‘Euphoria’ Makeup Artist Used Red Lips and Black Eyeliner to Reflect Jules’ Power, Maturity and Sexuality

title: ‘Hearing’ Review: Lê Bảo Continues His Sensory Exploration With an Arresting Study in Silence
description: In Vietnamese director Lê Bảo’s new film, an extended family confronts various rifts and estrangements in its ranks; years of silence must give way,
body:
In Vietnamese director Lê Bảo’s new film, an extended family confronts various rifts and estrangements in its ranks; years of silence must give way, slowly and haltingly, to communication. That the film is called “Hearing” might sound awfully pat, but nothing is so obvious in this sensuous, intuitive mood piece, which consistently surprises with its spare, searching narrative and radically layered technique. In his second feature — following 2021’s highly accomplished “Taste,” which won a jury prize in Berlin’s former Encounters competition — Lê continues to invite comparisons with rigorously experimental formalists like Apichatpong Weerasethakul and Pedro Costa, while cutting a path between closely observed domestic drama and freely ambient surrealism that feels his own. 
	

	Premiering in the main competition at Locarno, this is challenging arthouse fare of the type that may need continued festival exposure and accolades to persuade distributors to take a chance on it. “Hearing” could have an easier route to specialist streaming platforms, though its exquisite technical qualities — in particular, Vincent Villa’s intricate sound design — are best showcased in theaters. Singapore production company E&W Films’ recent credits include Cannes selections “Viet and Nam” and “9 Temples to Heaven,” which is a fair indication of the new film’s woozy, hypnotic slow-cinema lane.


	As indicated by the titles of his two features to date (plus the 2014 short “Scent”), Lê’s cinema is sense-led, and a bravura opening sequence establishes this film’s reliance on sonic texture and contrast. In a packed, bustling restaurant, collective chatter reaches cacophonous levels, which is where mechanic Ninh (Nguyễn Quốc Tuấn) comes in. His job is the installation of decibel meters, which trigger a glaring blue light when excessive levels of noise are reached — as happens here, though the rowdy patrons aren’t deterred. We cut away to a florist above the establishment, where workers stand taut in stark half-light, as if petrified by the din below; only when one neighbor, driven to breaking point, throws a flower pot off the balcony is there a brief, blessed, slightly bemused hush.
	

	But noise is release in this dusty working-class community, where lives tend to unfold in unassuming quiet. We see that cathartic shift in volume again at a local nightclub on the edge of the forest, where villagers of all ages dance manically to deep, throbbing techno music — Ninh among them. His days are altogether more muted: He lives with his elderly mother (Ngọc Tản), following his separation from his wife (Khánh Huyền), who has moved with their two children to her parents’ house nearby. He yearns to reconcile, but she can’t forgive his past domestic violence. Ninh’s parents’ marriage was destroyed by similar abuse, though in their case, it’s his rural-dwelling father (Minh Hùng), the perpetrator, who refuses to make peace.

	Silence is not calm in “Hearing,” however, and it’s certainly not contentment. Lê’s film is marked throughout by wounded reticence and nervous distance, and conversation, when it comes, doesn’t break the tension. Ninh’s mother awkwardly reminisces to him about her physical relationship with his father; Ninh frankly and regretfully tells his children about how he beat their mother. In work, at least, quiet is productive and purposeful: In some of the film’s most mesmerising scenes, we observe as basket-weavers methodically ply their trade, or mushroom farmers water the hay bales on which the fungi are cultivated. 

	Lê is interested in all the activity that fills a day, in its movement and sound, and attentive to the busy ecosystem that surrounds and sustains his principal characters. On occasion, we drift from human life altogether, fixating instead on the chatter of monkeys gathered in a mangrove forest, and for a time, serenity sets in. DP Nguyễn Vinh Phúc shoots all these tableaux — natural or domestic, pained or peaceful — with equally watchful, exacting composure and deep-shadowed still-life lighting. We’re certainly invited to peer into these frames, for flickers of buried human feeling or stray signs of the uncanny, but “Hearing” encourages the kind of stillness that puts, well, hearing first: Lê’s gorgeous, secretive film demands you lean in and listen to it.

schema.headline: ‘Hearing’ Review: Lê Bảo Continues His Sensory Exploration With an Arresting Study in Silence

title: Can Jean Smart Become the First Woman in Emmy History to Sweep Every Season of Her Series?
description: Winning an Emmy is hard. Winning one for every eligible season of a television series is almost impossible, and has never happened for a woman … unt
body:
Winning an Emmy is hard. Winning one for every eligible season of a television series is almost impossible, and has never happened for a woman … until now? 

	Jean Smart has won lead comedy actress for every eligible season of HBO Max’s “Hacks,” taking home trophies in 2021, 2022, 2024, and 2025. With the acclaimed comedy ending after its fifth season, Smart is nominated one final time. A fifth consecutive win would complete a flawless run across the series’ entire life span, something no woman has ever achieved in the acting categories. The victory would carry added significance for Smart’s own legacy. It would be her eighth career Emmy, moving her into a tie with Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman for the second most acting Emmys won by a female performer.
	

	Noteworthy, Allison Janney, a supporting drama actress nominee for “The Diplomat,” can also join Zendaya, who has won two Emmys for playing Rue on “Euphoria.” 08.10.2026 3 Variety the elite list if she wins as she’s tied with Smart and Mary Tyler Moore. Should Smart fall short, however, she would finish with the same agonizing near miss that befell Louis-Dreyfus, who won six Emmys across the seven-season run of “Veep.”


	So, who can stop Smart in her tracks? Her HBO Max counterpart, Lisa Kudrow, who has the most remarkable streak of all, earning noms for every season of cringe-comedy “The Comeback” in 2006, 2015 and now 2026 — a perfect run stretched across two decades. A previous winner for “Friends,” and also a nominee with cowriter Michael Patrick King, there could be a groundswell of support to give her a trophy, similar to the performer that beat Louis-Dreyfus in 2019: Phoebe Waller-Bridge for “Fleabag.”
	

	When you’re looking at the other woman seeking to make history, Zendaya’s streak is shorter but no less remarkable, and arguably more difficult to sustain in her competitive field. She won lead drama actress for the first two seasons of “Euphoria” in 2020 and 2022, becoming the youngest two-time Emmy winner in history. Now, after the show’s lengthy hiatus, she returns with a chance to remain undefeated for a third time, but with mixed reviews, and two deniable powerhouses — Rhea Seehorn from “Pluribus” and Keri Russell from “The Diplomat” — she has her work cut out for her.

	But why does any of this matter? Because Emmy history tells us this hardly ever happens. Only Bill Cosby has won an acting Emmy for every season of a scripted series that lasted at least three seasons, sweeping all three installments of “I Spy” from 1966 through 1968. (Blythe Danner accomplished the feat on “Huff,” but that Showtime drama lasted only two seasons.) A victory by either Smart or Zendaya would end a drought that has lasted nearly six decades and would mark the first woman to achieve the milestone.

	Looking strictly at nominations, the list grows considerably, with 39 performers earning Emmy nominations for every eligible season of a show’s full run. They include legends such as 11-time nominees Alan Alda (“MASH”), Ted Danson (“Cheers”) and David Hyde Pierce (“Frasier”), along with eight-time nominees Peter Dinklage (“Game of Thrones”), Jon Hamm (“Mad Men”) and Tony Shalhoub (“Monk”), plus seven-time perfect streaks from Julia Louis-Dreyfus (“Veep”), Alec Baldwin and Tina Fey (“30 Rock”), Jane Kaczmarek (“Malcolm in the Middle”), Helen Hunt (“Mad About You”), Betty White and Estelle Getty (“The Golden Girls”), Betty Thomas (“Hill Street Blues”) and Mary Tyler Moore and Ed Asner (“The Mary Tyler Moore Show”).

	That so few have managed it speaks to how brutal the arithmetic of television can be. A show must stay great, stay on the air and remain in the Television Academy’s good graces for years, all while its lead performer fends off an ever-changing field of challengers every awards cycle.

	Even sustaining a perfect nomination streak is extraordinarily rare, and this year proved how quickly one could unravel. “The Bear” delivered the cycle’s cruelest shock: Two-time winners Jeremy Allen White and Ebon Moss-Bachrach, nominated for every previous season, were shut out completely, leaving Ayo Edebiri as the show’s lone acting nominee. Interestingly, previous guest comedy actor winner Jon Bernthal had also been nominated for every season of the show before his streak ended on nomination morning. Sheryl Lee Ralph, flawless through four seasons of “Abbott Elementary,” also saw her streak snapped, one year after co-star Tyler James Williams suffered the same fate before returning to the lineup this year.
	

	This year’s Emmy nominees include several performers who have been recognized for every season of their current series. Quinta Brunson and Janelle James are each five for five for “Abbott Elementary.” Hannah Einbinder has matched Smart with nominations for all five seasons of “Hacks.” Martin Short has been nominated for every season of “Only Murders in the Building” without breaking through for a win, while Jason Segel and Jessica Williams are each three for three for “Shrinking,” though neither is widely viewed as a front-runner.

	“The Diplomat” star Russell is also on a perfect run through the show’s first three seasons, making her a legitimate spoiler after her Actor Awards victory. And let’s not forget that next year could bring back several active perfect streaks following hiatuses: the “Ted Lasso” quartet of Jason Sudeikis, Brett Goldstein, Hannah Waddingham and Juno Temple, along with the possibility of “Severance” stars Adam Scott, John Turturro and Patricia Arquette extending their own runs.

	That’s what makes Smart’s and Zendaya’s pursuits so compelling. A perfect Emmy streak exists only until the season it doesn’t. One missed nomination or one loss is all it takes to erase the possibility forever, forcing a performer to start over with an entirely new series. Both women already rank among the most decorated performers of their generations. What’s on the table now is something even scarcer than another statuette: A chance to finish with an unblemished Emmy record that could outlive a career.

	This week’s updated Emmy winner predictions are below.



	

					Zendaya in “Euphoria” (HBO Max)

title: Trump Media, Operator of Truth Social, Reports Q2 Net Loss of $238.1 Million and Revenue of $1.7 Million
description: Trump Media & Technology Group posted another large net loss for the second quarter of 2026, of $238.1 million, while the company generated $1.7 mil
body:
Trump Media & Technology Group posted another large net loss for the second quarter of 2026, of $238.1 million, while the company generated $1.7 million in sales for the period.

	Donald Trump is the largest shareholder in TMTG, holding more than 40% of its shares through a revocable trust, according to a July 21 Bloomberg report. The company operates Truth Social, President Trump’s favored social media platform.


	The company $238.1 million net loss for the June quarter compares with a $20 million net loss in the year-earlier period. TMTG said the “vast bulk” of its losses in Q2 of 2026 were “non-cash losses,” including unrealized losses on digital assets, digital assets pledged and equity securities ($190.4 million). The company reported $25.6 million in legal expenses in the most recent quarter, primarily related to “legacy litigation” that has now been “substantially resolved.” TMTG’s $1.7 million in revenue was up 89% from $883,300 generated in the second quarter of 2025.
	

	TMTG said it ended Q2 with total assets of $2.0 billion and financial assets of approximately $1.9 billion comprising cash, restricted cash, short-term investments, equity securities, note receivable and accrued interest, digital assets and digital assets pledged.

	On Aug. 1, TMTG launched a new “Truth API” service that provides instant access to “the highest-ranking” accounts on Truth Social — including Trump’s — charging as much as $100,000 per month. The move has drawn criticism from both Democrats and Republicans, including Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), who called it “a form of buying access.” In announcing earnings Monday, TMTG said it had “onboarded a number of institutional customers prior to its August 1, 2026, launch and, despite receiving what it believes to be factually inaccurate criticism of Truth API, is continuing to onboard additional partners.”
	

	TMTG says its mission is “to end Big Tech’s assault on free speech by opening up the Internet and giving people their voices back.” The company was founded in February 2021 after Trump was suspended from platforms including Twitter (now called X), Facebook, Instagram and YouTube; those services said Trump had violated rules against inciting violence in connection with the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol.

	In December 2025, Trump Media announced a merger agreement with nuclear fusion company TAE Technologies in an all-stock deal valued at more than $6 billion. The companies had expected to close the transaction by mid-2026; on Monday, TMTG said the TAE merger is targeted to close in Q4 2026.

	“Over the past few months, we’ve sharpened our strategic direction and brought real discipline to how we allocate capital,” TMTG interim CEO Kevin McGurn, a former Hulu exec, said in a statement. “We’re making meaningful progress toward our proposed merger with TAE Technologies, which we believe is the most important driver of long-term shareholder value and a natural extension of our commitment to building durable, un-cancelable infrastructure, this time in energy security. At the same time, we’ve refined our approach to capital allocation to better direct resources to the core pillars of our media business, and that effort is already yielding results.”

	Meanwhile, on Aug. 7, TMTG and Yorkville Acquisition Corp. (a blank-check company incorporated in the Cayman Islands set up for the purposes of M&A) announced an agreement to “mutually terminate their previously announced proposed business combination to establish Trump Media Group CRO Strategy, Inc.” — which had been described as a “digital asset treasury company focused on acquisition of the native cryptocurrency token of the Cronos ecosystem (‘CRO’)” — citing “prevailing market conditions” and “shifting business and stakeholder priorities.” In addition, Crypto.com, Trump Media and Yorkville America mutually agreed not to pursue their previously announced partnership, under which Crypto.com was to service certain of Yorkville America’s anticipated electronically traded fund (ETF) offerings.

	Originally, TMTG and Crypto.com’s agreement called for Trump Media to introduce a rewards system on the Truth Social and Truth+ platforms that used Crypto.com’s digital wallet infrastructure and that adopted the CRO digital currency as a utility token. In a joint press release last Friday, TMTG and Crypto.com said: “Rather than develop a direct prediction market integration on Truth Social, the companies will pivot to a marketing agreement under which Crypto.com’s prediction markets experiences will be marketed to the Truth Social user base.”

title: Chud The Builder Released From Jail After Two Months Behind Bars
description:
Chud The Builder
                          Back On The Streets After 2 Months In Jail
body:
Chud The Builder
                          Back On The Streets After 2 Months In Jail
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            7:42 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 10, 2026
                                10:25 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Chud The Builder is tasting freedom after two months in a Tennessee jail ... TMZ has confirmed he posted bond and has been released.
      
    
            The streamer -- real name Dalton Eatherly -- was released Monday morning from the Montgomery County Jail ... two months after a judge set his bond at $1 million.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A rep for the Montgomery County Circuit Criminal Court tells TMZ ... Chud posted $1 million bond and he had 10 bail bonds services each cover $100,000. We're told Chud put up 10% of his bond.
      
    
            Chud was behind bars after being charged with attempted murder in connection with a May 13 shooting outside a Montgomery County courthouse.
      
    
            As we reported ... cops say Chud shot a man, and he claims he was jumped outside the courthouse and fired in self-defense. Chud also claims he accidentally shot himself in the chaos, and we have photos of him being wheeled away on a stretcher.
      
    
            Chud is also facing a criminal case out of Davidson County ... he was arrested a few days before the shooting for allegedly causing a scene inside a Nashville steakhouse, walking out on a nearly $400 tab.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Prosecutors charged him with theft of services, disorderly conduct, and resisting arrest.
      
    
            Both cases have been sent to a grand jury for review ... according to WSMV.

title: Brad Pitt Says He's Drinking Alcohol Again After Seven Years Sober
description:
Brad Pitt
                          I'm Drinking Again After 7 Years Sober
body:
Brad Pitt
                          I'm Drinking Again After 7 Years Sober
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            7:03 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 10, 2026
                                1:25 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brad Pitt says his seven-year run of sobriety is over ... he's drinking again, though he insists he's learned he still needs to keep a tight leash on things.
      
    
            The actor opened up in a wide-ranging interview with Esquire ... saying, "I was sober for seven years. And then I got back off the wagon" -- quickly adding he's drinking "in a more restrained manner."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brad admitted he got overconfident a couple of times and quickly realized drinking in large quantities still isn't good for him.
      
    
            He says he can have a few glasses of wine ... but not too many, explaining, "I have to be professional about it."
      

        
                    
                      JANUARY 2020
                  
      
    
            As we previously reported ... Brad previously credited Bradley Cooper with helping him get sober after his split from Angelina Jolie. He also spent more than a year attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings during that period.
      
    
            The conversation took a much darker turn ... as Brad reflected on a painful period involving what he would only describe as "family stuff."
      
    
            Brad said suicide generally wasn't in his makeup ... but acknowledged there was one period when the pain became so "oppressive" he understood how someone could view death as relief. He stressed he never planned to act on those thoughts, and said his survival instincts quickly kicked in.
      
    
            When the interviewer asked whether the period involved his children, Brad declined to elaborate ... repeating, "Family stuff. We could leave it at that."
      
    
            As Brad put it ... "This s*** ain't easy" -- even for a guy who says he "won the lottery."
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

title: Influencer Sofia Murillo Dies In Helicopter Crash With Mom, Grandma in Brazil
description:
Influencer Sofia Murillo
                          Dead at 17 In Helicopter Crash ...
body:
Influencer Sofia Murillo
                          Dead at 17 In Helicopter Crash ...
                          Mom, Grandma Killed Too
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            9:43 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Three generations of one family -- a 17-year-old influencer, her mother and her grandmother -- died in a fiery helicopter crash in Brazil ... while their relatives waited at the hangar for the next flight.
      
    
            Sofia Murillo boarded the sightseeing helicopter in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday with her mother, Wendy Manrique, and grandmother, Rocio Cubillos. Pilot Alessandro Rocha was also aboard -- all were killed.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Sofia had more than 250,000 followers across Instagram and TikTok, where she shared beauty advice and cosmetic reviews.
      

            Her final post came three days before the crash.
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            The family was vacationing in Brazil and booked a 20-minute flight to see the iconic Christ the Redeemer statue.
      
    
            Because the helicopter could only carry three passengers, the family split into groups. Sofia, her mom, and grandmother took off first around 11 AM.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sofia's uncle, his wife and the couple's 15-year-old daughter remained at the hangar ... and her uncle told local outlets they learned about the crash from news reports while waiting for their turn.
      
    
            The helicopter went down in a remote, wooded area and burst into flames ... complicating rescue efforts.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The crash remains under investigation ... but the tour company claims the helicopter's maintenance was current, the business had the required permit, and the pilot was properly licensed.
      
    
            The fatal crash comes less than two months after Oliver Tree died in a helicopter collision -- also in Rio de Janeiro.
      
    
            RIP

            Kristen Stewart is taking movie promotion to a higher level ... popping a THC gummy before Korean BBQ ... and letting the munchies handle the rest.
      
    
            The 'Wrong Girls' star joined viral foodie Natasha Zhatko -- better known online as natashahasthemunchies -- for her latest baked bite, she's hitting Soot Bull Jip in L.A.'s Koreatown after taking gummies outside.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Kristen says she's happy to be doing movie promo with somebody else who's "high and awkward" ... admitting she's usually the only one bringing that energy.
      

            Her costar, Alia Shawkat, is also along for the ride ... taking charge of the barbecue while the gummies seemingly take charge of the conversation.
      
    
            The chatter drifts from how Kristen and Alia got their start to pork blood and other smoky subjects ... before Natasha reveals her dream guests are Martha Stewart and Snoop Dogg.
      
    
            Natasha eventually asks the question "everybody wants to know" ... whether Kristen and Alia have officially been invited into the Illuminati ... and the pair actually gives a response.
      
    
            "The Wrong Girls" hits theaters August 14 ... and these two are promoting it on a high note.
